description: Return the existing CmpInst when predicate, LHS and RHS exactly equal requested predicate and operand order.
extra: condition of V is a CmpInst; exact predicate and operand pointer identity

description: Return the existing CmpInst when its predicate is the requested predicate’s swapped form and its operands are exactly reversed.
extra: condition of V is a CmpInst; swapped predicate and reversed operand pointer identity

description: For an unsigned/equality pointer comparison only, strip accumulated constant offsets (allowing non-inbounds GEPs only for equality); when both pointers reduce to the identical base, compare the offsets with the signed-converted predicate and return that boolean constant.
extra: DataLayout pointer index size; accumulated constant GEP offsets

description: For an equality comparison between bases proven to have non-overlapping storage, if both bases have known non-null object sizes and the difference between offsets is strictly within either object (not merely one-past), fold to the predicate's unequal-pointer result.
extra: non-overlapping storage proof; object-size/dereferenceable bytes and nullability; offset distance

description: For pointer equality, if every underlying object on one side is a noalias allocation call and every underlying object on the other is statically/dispositionally allocation-disjoint (in either operand order), fold to unequal.
extra: getUnderlyingObjects; noalias call and allocation-disjoint classification

description: For pointer equality, if an operand is an alloc-like call and the other operand is known nonzero, and the allocation pointer is not captured (except comparisons to a pointer loaded from a global), fold to the predicate's false-when-equal result. Upstream marks this rule FIXME/PR54002 because the fold may not be valid for all comparisons to that address.
extra: TargetLibraryInfo alloc-like classification; known-nonzero; pointer capture tracking

description: For i1 operands with RHS 0, fold `icmp ne X, 0`, `icmp ugt X, 0`, or `icmp slt X, 0` to X.
extra: LHS and RHS are i1 scalar/vector; RHS is zero

description: For i1 operands with RHS 0, fold `icmp eq|ule|sge (not X), 0` to X when LHS matches bitwise-not of X.
extra: LHS is a recognized bitwise not; RHS is zero

description: For i1 operands with RHS 0, `icmp ult X,0` and `icmp sgt X,0` are false.

description: For i1 operands with RHS 0, `icmp uge X,0` and `icmp sle X,0` are true.

description: For i1 operands with RHS 1, fold `icmp eq|uge|sle X,1` to X.

description: For i1 operands with RHS 1, fold `icmp ne|ult|sgt (not X),1` to X when LHS matches bitwise-not of X.

description: For i1 operands with RHS 1, `icmp ugt X,1` and `icmp slt X,1` are false.

description: For i1 operands with RHS 1, `icmp ule X,1` and `icmp sge X,1` are true.

description: For i1 operands and predicate ULE, return true when LHS logically implies RHS.

description: For i1 operands and predicate SLE, return true when RHS logically implies LHS.

description: For `icmp` sign-bit checks on `bitcast(uitofp X)`, return the boolean indicated by `isSignBitCheck(Pred,C,TrueIfSigned)` (the source folds unsigned-to-FP results that cannot be negative).

description: If the exact ICmp region for constant C is empty, every value fails the comparison, so fold false.
extra: RHS is APInt constant; ConstantRange::makeExactICmpRegion is empty

description: If the exact ICmp region for constant C is the full set, every value passes, so fold true.
extra: RHS is APInt constant; ConstantRange::makeExactICmpRegion is full

description: If LHS has a non-full computed range wholly contained in the exact true region of comparison with C, fold true.
extra: RHS APInt constant; computeConstantRange(LHS,signedness) is not full; RHS region contains LHS range

description: If LHS has a non-full computed range wholly contained in the inverse region of comparison with C, fold false.
extra: RHS APInt constant; computeConstantRange(LHS,signedness) is not full; inverse RHS region contains LHS range

description: For EQ/NE of a nuw or nsw multiplication by nonzero constant MulC against C, fold when C is not divisible by MulC: NE→true and EQ→false.
extra: UseInstrInfo enabled; multiplication carries NUW with unsigned remainder nonzero or NSW with signed remainder nonzero; EQ/NE

description: `icmp uge X,1` is true when X is known nonzero.
extra: Predicate UGE; C exactly one; LHS known nonzero

description: For UGE or ULT, collect depth-at-most-one unsigned lower/upper bounds through OR, saturating add/sub, AND, URem, UDiv, LShr, and nuw multiplication (the latter only when the other factor is known nonzero); if an identical value occurs in both bound sets, fold UGE true or ULT false.
extra: depth-limited monotonic-value analysis, saturation intrinsics, nuw flags and known-nonzero

description: For `icmp slt (or X,Y), X`, return true if KnownBits proves X nonnegative and Y negative; for `icmp sge` under the same facts, return false.
extra: RHS is identical to one OR operand; KnownBits sign facts

description: For `icmp slt (or X,Y), X`, return false if X is negative or Y is nonnegative; for `icmp sge` under those facts, return true.
extra: RHS is identical to one OR operand; KnownBits sign facts

description: For `(urem X,Y) == Y`, `(urem X,Y) >u Y`, or `(urem X,Y) >=u Y`, fold false. Also fold signed `>s`/`>=s` false when Y is proven nonnegative.
extra: RHS equals URem divisor; signed predicates additionally require KnownBits nonnegative for Y

description: For `(urem X,Y) != Y`, `(urem X,Y) <u Y`, or `(urem X,Y) <=u Y`, fold true. Also fold signed `<s`/`<=s` true when Y is proven nonnegative.
extra: RHS equals URem divisor; signed predicates additionally require KnownBits nonnegative for Y

description: For nonzero X, fold `(X lshr C) == X`, `(X lshr C) >=u X`, `(X lshr C) >u X`, and corresponding `udiv X,C` comparisons false.
extra: Shift amount C≠0 for lshr or divisor C≠1 for udiv; RHS X known nonzero

description: For nonzero X, fold `(X lshr C) != X`, `(X lshr C) <u X`, `(X lshr C) <=u X`, and corresponding `udiv X,C` comparisons true.
extra: Shift amount C≠0 for lshr or divisor C≠1 for udiv; RHS X known nonzero

description: Fold `icmp ugt E, X` false when E is one of `(X*C1) udiv C2` with C1≤uC2, `(X*C1) lshr C2` with C1≤u2^C2, or `(X shl C1) udiv C2` with 2^C1≤uC2.
extra: All constants; APInt unsigned inequalities exactly as stated

description: Fold `icmp ule E, X` true when E is one of `(X*C1) udiv C2` with C1≤uC2, `(X*C1) lshr C2` with C1≤u2^C2, or `(X shl C1) udiv C2` with 2^C1≤uC2.
extra: All constants; APInt unsigned inequalities exactly as stated

description: Fold `(sub C,X) == X` false and `(sub C,X) != X` true when C is an odd APInt constant.
extra: RHS is the subtrahend X; C odd; EQ or NE

description: Schema: signed relational comparison of X+C1 and X+C2 where exactly the RHS add has NSW (after canonicalizing it to RHS); reduce to comparing C1 and C2 if (C1≤sC2 and C1≥s0) or (C2≤sC1 and C1≤s0).
extra: NSW flag on one add and signed APInt comparisons

description: Reduce `icmp pred (X+Y), X` to the recursive comparison `icmp pred Y, 0` when the addend X matches either add operand and predicate/add flags make wrapping irrelevant.
extra: MaxRecurse>0; equality predicate or add has required NUW for unsigned predicate / NSW for signed predicate; recursive result non-null

description: Reduce `icmp pred X, (X+Y)` to recursive `icmp pred 0,Y` when X matches either RHS add operand and predicate/add flags make wrapping irrelevant.
extra: MaxRecurse>0; equality predicate or add has required NUW/NSW; recursive result non-null

description: For `icmp pred (A+B),(C+D)` with any one shared add operand, cancel the common term and recursively compare the two remaining addends.
extra: MaxRecurse>0; at least one SSA operand shared; both adds safe for predicate via equality/no-wrap flags or trySimplifyICmpWithAdds; recursive result non-null

description: If LHS is a BinaryOperator, delegate comparison simplification to simplifyICmpWithBinOpOnLHS and return its first successful result. The concrete binop rules are separate entries.
extra: MaxRecurse; helper result

description: If RHS is a BinaryOperator, swap the ICmp predicate and operands and delegate to simplifyICmpWithBinOpOnLHS; return its first successful result. The concrete binop rules are separate entries.
extra: MaxRecurse; swapped predicate; helper result

description: For signed `icmp slt` or `icmp ne` of `0 - (zext X)` against positive C, return true.
extra: Predicate signed; C strictly positive

description: For signed `icmp sge` or `icmp eq` of `0 - (zext X)` against positive C, return false.
extra: Predicate signed; C strictly positive

description: For signed `icmp sle` of `0 - (zext X)` against nonnegative C, return true.
extra: Predicate signed; C nonnegative

description: For signed `icmp sgt` of `0 - (zext X)` against nonnegative C, return false.
extra: Predicate signed; C nonnegative

description: Fold `(C2 shl X) == C` false when C2 is a power of two, C is a non-power-of-two constant, and the shift cannot erase the one bit under the safety guard.
extra: NSW or NUW on shift, or C2==1, or C!=0; predicate EQ

description: Fold `(C2 shl X) != C` true when C2 is a power of two, C is a non-power-of-two constant, and the shift cannot erase the one bit under the safety guard.
extra: NSW or NUW on shift, or C2==1, or C!=0; predicate NE

description: For power-of-two C, `(C shl X) >u signmask` is false.
extra: RHS is sign-mask constant; predicate UGT

description: For power-of-two C, `(C shl X) <=u signmask` is true.
extra: RHS is sign-mask constant; predicate ULE

description: For two `shl` results with identical left operand, recursively compare their shift amounts when both shifts have NUW, signed comparisons also have NSW on both, and the common left operand is known nonzero.
extra: MaxRecurse>0; both shifts NUW; signed predicates require both NSW; common input known nonzero; recursive result non-null

description: For matching `(X and C1)`/`(X and C2)` or `(X or C1)`/`(X or C2)`, fold ULE true when one constant bitmask is a subset of the other after operand/predicate canonicalization.
extra: Same opcode and first operand; relational predicate; constant masks; C1 subset C2

description: For matching `(X and C1)`/`(X and C2)` or `(X or C1)`/`(X or C2)`, fold UGT false when one constant bitmask is a subset of the other after operand/predicate canonicalization.
extra: Same opcode and first operand; relational predicate; constant masks; C1 subset C2

description: For matching AND/OR constant-mask results, fold SLE true when the canonicalized mask constants are subset-related and have the same sign classification.
extra: Same opcode and first operand; relational predicate; constants; subset relation and equal nonnegative/sign-bit status

description: For matching AND/OR constant-mask results, fold SGT false when the canonicalized mask constants are subset-related and have the same sign classification.
extra: Same opcode and first operand; relational predicate; constants; subset relation and equal nonnegative/sign-bit status

description: For exact UDiv or LShr results with the same divisor/shift amount, recursively compare their numerators when the predicate is unsigned.
extra: MaxRecurse>0; same opcode and second operand; both instructions exact; predicate unsigned; recursive result non-null

description: For exact SDiv results with the same divisor, recursively compare their numerators only for EQ/NE.
extra: MaxRecurse>0; same opcode and second operand; both exact; EQ or NE; recursive result non-null

description: For exact AShr results with the same shift amount, recursively compare their inputs.
extra: MaxRecurse>0; same opcode and second operand; both exact; recursive result non-null

description: For Shl results with the same shift amount, recursively compare their inputs when both shifts have NUW or both have NSW; signed predicates require NSW on both.

description: After canonicalizing a signed smax/smin comparison against one of its own operands to `max(A,B) pred A` or its swapped-predicate equivalent for min, when P is EQ/SLE, return the comparison already used as condition by the LHS select if it exactly tests `A EqP B` (EqP is SGE for smax, SLE for smin).

description: After canonicalizing a signed smax/smin comparison against one of its own operands to `max(A,B) pred A` or its swapped-predicate equivalent for min, when P is EQ/SLE, otherwise reuse a matching `A EqP B` condition from the RHS select.

description: After canonicalizing a signed smax/smin comparison against one of its own operands to `max(A,B) pred A` or its swapped-predicate equivalent for min, when P is EQ/SLE, recursively simplify `icmp EqP A,B` and return it if it folds.

description: After canonicalizing a signed smax/smin comparison against one of its own operands to `max(A,B) pred A` or its swapped-predicate equivalent for min, when P is NE/SGT, return the LHS select condition if it exactly tests `A inverse(EqP) B`.

description: After canonicalizing a signed smax/smin comparison against one of its own operands to `max(A,B) pred A` or its swapped-predicate equivalent for min, when P is NE/SGT, otherwise reuse a matching `A inverse(EqP) B` condition from the RHS select.

description: After canonicalizing an unsigned umax/umin comparison against one of its own operands to `max(A,B) pred A` or its swapped-predicate equivalent for min, when P is NE/UGT, return the LHS select condition if it exactly tests `A inverse(EqP) B`.

description: After canonicalizing an unsigned umax/umin comparison against one of its own operands to `max(A,B) pred A` or its swapped-predicate equivalent for min, when P is NE/UGT, otherwise reuse a matching `A inverse(EqP) B` condition from the RHS select.

description: For signed `smax(A,B)` versus `smin(C,D)` sharing any operand, `smax(A,B) sge smin(C,D)` is true.

description: If a dominating, context-valid llvm.assume implies the queried comparison, replace it with the implied boolean result; the compare operands must be among the assumption bases and the assumption must validate for the current context.

description: For EQ or NE with an undef RHS, return undef because it can be chosen to make either outcome hold.

description: `icmp pred X,X` folds to the predicate's truth value on equal operands. The distinct undef operand alternative is IS3918u.
extra: LHS equals RHS or RHS is undef

description: `icmp pred X,undef` folds to the predicate's truth value on equal operands for non-equality predicates. EQ/NE with undef are handled earlier by IS3913.
extra: LHS equals RHS or RHS is undef

description: For same-address-width `ptrtoint/ptrtoaddr(P)` and `ptrtoint/ptrtoaddr(Q)` with equal source pointer types, recursively compare P and Q with same predicate.

description: For `icmp pred (zext X),(zext Y)` with equal source types, recursively compare X and Y using the unsigned form of pred.

description: For same-source `(zext X) ule (sext X)` or `(zext X) sge (sext X)`, fold true.

description: For same-source `(zext X) ugt (sext X)` or `(zext X) slt (sext X)`, fold false.

description: For `(zext X) pred C` when truncation followed by zext changes C (so RHS has nonzero upper bits), predicates EQ, UGT and UGE are false.

description: For `(zext X) pred C` when truncation followed by zext changes C, predicates NE, ULT and ULE are true.

description: For `(zext X) slt|sle C` when C does not fit in source width, return the constant result of `C sge 0` (nonnegative C means true, negative C false).

description: For same-source `(sext X) uge (zext X)` or `(sext X) sle (zext X)`, fold true.

description: For `(sext X) eq C` when truncation and re-extension changes C, fold false.

description: For `(sext X) ne C` when truncation and re-extension changes C, fold true.

description: For `(sext X) sgt|sge C` when C does not fit source width, return the constant result of `C slt 0`.

description: For `(sext X) slt|sle C` when C does not fit source width, return the constant result of `C sge 0`.
